How to Buy Properties at 40-90% Below Market Value with Los Angeles County, California Tax Deed Investing

Los Angeles County is the most populous county in the United States, with an estimated 9.7 million residents as of 2022. This large population makes it one of the prime markets for deed auctions. The robust economy, increasing population, and favourable climate make LA County an attractive spot for real estate investors. However, it’s also one of the most expensive markets.

One of the smartest ways to enter the LA real estate market is through a tax deed auction, where you can potentially acquire property ownership for a fraction of the market value.

The Opportunity of LA County Tax Deed Auctions

Every year, LA County auctions off properties that have defaulted on their taxes, providing a unique opportunity for investors. These tax sales help the county reclaim lost revenue, which is vital for funding public services.

The starting bid for these properties is set to cover the unpaid taxes, fees, and associated costs. Plus, these properties are typically free of mortgages or deed of trust loans, offering a clean slate in an otherwise pricey market. It’s a win-win for both you and the county.

Getting Started with LA County Tax Deed Auctions

So, how do you begin in LA County? It all starts with the Los Angeles Treasurer and Tax Collector’s website.

Here’s a step-by-step guide:

  1. Visit the Los Angeles Treasurer and Tax Collector’s Website
    • Navigate to the “Auction Information” section.
  2. Check the Schedule of Upcoming Auctions
    • This will direct you to the Bid for Assets auction site. Review the auction rules, register online, and submit a refundable deposit.
  3. Read the Participation Guide
    • On the Bid for Assets auction site, read the “HOW TO PARTICIPATE IN COUNTY TAX SALES” section. Once registered, you’ll receive the auction list via email or direct download from the website.
  4. Get the Auction List
    • The list of tax-delinquent properties becomes available a few weeks before the auction, usually scheduled in October. This is your crucial first step in preparing a winning bid.

Before participating, make sure to do thorough research by exploring the LA County Assessor Portal and the Bid for Assets site.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a tax deed auction?

A tax deed auction is a public sale of properties that have defaulted on their taxes. The county sells these properties to recover the unpaid taxes.

How can I participate in the LA County tax deed auction?

You can participate by registering on the Los Angeles Treasurer and Tax Collector’s website and the Bid for Assets auction site. Follow the instructions provided for registration and deposit submission.

Are the properties free of mortgages?

Yes, properties sold at these auctions are typically free of mortgages or deed of trust loans, giving buyers a clean slate.

When do these auctions take place?

The auctions usually take place in October, with the auction list available a few weeks before the scheduled date.

Where can I find more information?

You can find more information on the Los Angeles Treasurer and Tax Collector’s website and the Bid for Assets auction site.

Auction FAQs

I would like to get notification about upcoming auctions in LA County. What do I need to do?

Subscribe to Auction Email Notification.

How can I obtain a list of properties scheduled for an auction?

You can review and print the list of “Properties Remaining for Sale” for a specific auction under the Schedule of Upcoming Auctions page.

What are known special conditions?

Special conditions such as contamination, easements, or Mello-Roos apply to certain properties. It’s important for buyers to do their due diligence as properties are sold as is, and the Treasurer and Tax Collector do not assume responsibility for the conditions, liens, environmental hazards, or any other special conditions.

I would like to bid on properties offered at an auction. Are there different bidding requirements for an in-person auction versus an online auction?

Yes, there are different bidding requirements for an in-person auction versus an online auction. Please review “Terms and Conditions” for a specific auction, under the Schedule of Upcoming Auctions page.

How do I find or see a property that I would like to bid on at an auction?

The Office of the Assessor provides property information, including maps that you can access at the Los Angeles County Office of the Assessor. Enter the property street number and street name, or the Assessor Identification Number, to find the property details. For properties without street addresses, the approximate geographic location can be determined using County Assessor Platt maps and GIS maps, also found on the Assessor’s website at the Los Angeles County Office of the Assessor. Only a property survey can determine the exact boundary lines of a property. Interested bidders must bear the expense and receive permission from the owner to access the property.

Handy Research Tools

  • Zillow
  • Redfin

These sites are invaluable for digging deeper into your chosen property, from its exact location to boundary specifics. Conduct thorough due diligence, consult with experts, and get ready both financially and knowledge-wise for the auction.
